title: How It Works
subtitle: Two ways to work with Attolloo: a three-week assessment, and a board, advisory or mentoring role. Each has a defined scope and terms agreed before the work starts.

sections.heading: 1. Readiness Assessment
sections.body:
A review of your company as the people who have to say yes will see it: a regulated buyer, a regulator, a partner or an investor.

### What it covers

- The Responsible AI Gate: red lines, then misuse and dual-use risk on seven criteria
- The 6Sense screening across six dimensions
- An AI Compass baseline: where you stand on the questions buyers, regulators and investors ask about AI governance, security and suppliers
- Your EU AI Act classification, and what follows from it

### What you get

A written report with the findings, the two or three issues most likely to stop a deal, a licence or a funding round, and a 90-day plan in priority order. If the honest answer is that you are not ready yet, the report says so.

### Time and price

About three weeks from the first working session. Fixed price, quoted before we start.

[Book a Readiness Assessment](/contact.html#screening)

sections.heading: 2. Board, Advisory and Mentoring
sections.body:
A board seat, a standing advisory role or a mentoring agreement, for a fee agreed in advance.

BOARD MEMBER: governance structure, investor relations, and structured decisions on risk. Board-level accountability.

STRATEGIC ADVISER: a fixed number of days a month on the work the assessment identified, with deliverables agreed for each quarter.

MENTOR: regular one-to-one conversations with a founder or a leader about the decisions in front of them.

sections.heading: Why Fees Come First
sections.body: An adviser who works only for equity ends up choosing companies by what their shares might be worth. A fee for a defined piece of work keeps the first step small for you, and keeps my advice independent of whether we continue.

sections.heading: Who This Is For
sections.body:
Early-stage AI companies entering a regulated market, typically 12 to 36 months after first product launch. There are two kinds.

CHALLENGERS: companies that use AI to compete with the established players, in finance, insurance and other regulated services. They become the regulated party themselves, and have to convince a regulator, a partner and an investor.

SUPPLIERS: companies that sell AI to the established players. They have to get through the buyer's procurement and security review.

The sectors I know best:

- Fintech and Regtech: EU AI Act, DORA, MiFID II and GDPR as conditions for doing business
- Compliance automation: regulatory monitoring and governance documentation
- Cybersecurity services: NIS2, DORA and sector security requirements
- HR technology: AI in hiring and workforce management, high-risk under EU AI Act Annex III

### What falls outside

Companies outside regulated markets, hardware without a software governance layer, health and life science, and companies without paying customers. Any company that fails the [Responsible AI red-line check](/responsible-ai.html#the-responsible-ai-gate) is also excluded.

Attolloo does not take on companies that compete in the pension market, companies whose main customers are pension providers or the public sector, or companies that supply, or are bidding to supply, my current employer.
